answers.children: Glen of Imaal Terriers are moderately good with children when raised with them. Their tenacious and independent nature combined with a bold streak means they have low tolerance for being poked or pulled, so they suit older respectful kids better than toddlers. Living with this small but sturdy Irish terrier requires awareness of its scrappy personality to avoid clashes. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Glen of Imaal Terriers do not always get along with other pets. Bred for vermin control and small game hunting their strong prey drive leads to chasing small animals while independent stubbornness can create tension especially with same-sex dogs. Owners must manage these instincts or risk garden chaos and household friction.
answers.exercise: Glen of Imaal Terriers need around one hour of exercise daily. A mix of brisk walks and supervised backyard play suits their short sturdy legs and tenacious digging instinct but insufficient activity leaves them bored and destructive. Their history as silent workers in Ireland's hills shaped a moderate energy level that thrives on purposeful outlets.
answers.shedding: Yes — Glen of Imaal Terriers shed moderately with seasonal increases. Their medium double coat has a wiry texture that traps loose hair around the home especially during coat changes and requires regular brushing to prevent mats. This rugged coat from their Irish working heritage means vacuuming becomes part of daily life with the breed.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Glen of Imaal Terrier has a medium double coat that sheds lightly but still spreads dander and loose hair around the house. Its wiry outer layer and soft undercoat require regular hand-stripping to prevent matting, particularly on the sturdy legs bred for digging into Irish burrows. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic and the Glen of Imaal Terrier is not among those usually suggested to allergy sufferers. (PawLabs shedding score: 4/10)
answers.training: Glen of Imaal Terriers are not easy to train. Their independent and stubborn temperament combined with a history of working silently on vermin and badger hunting without constant human direction makes them slow to respond and prone to selective listening. This tenacious Irish terrier needs patient consistent handling to channel its intelligence productively.
answers.lifespan: Glen of Imaal Terriers live 10-15 years. Their rugged build from Ireland's harsh hills and overall health robustness support a typical terrier span but the breed's history of hard physical work means maintaining fitness helps them stay active into later years. Short sturdy legs and determined character define a compact dog that ages gracefully with proper care.
answers.size: Glen of Imaal Terriers reach 32-40 lb and stand 12-14 in at the shoulder. Their short sturdy legs and strong jaws give a surprisingly solid feel for such a small dog making them a compact but substantial presence around the house. This build from their vermin-hunting past allows them to dig and hold ground without being underfoot.
answers.barking: Glen of Imaal Terriers bark moderately rather than constantly. Bred to work silently on vermin and small game in Ireland they save their deep serious voice for alerting to intruders or exciting sights like squirrels instead of yapping. This selective barking fits their tenacious independent nature and avoids the noise common in other terriers.
answers.apartment: Glen of Imaal Terriers can live in an apartment with sufficient exercise and mental outlets. Their moderate energy moderate barking and ability to settle indoors suit smaller homes but the digging instinct and independent spirit demand daily activity and puzzle toys or they become restless. This rugged small breed from Ireland adapts if its working heritage is respected.
answers.first-time: Glen of Imaal Terriers are not ideal as a first dog. Their stubbornness slow trainability and strong prey drive from a history of badger hunting and vermin control demand experienced handling to manage digging chasing and independence. The affectionate loyalty shines once routines are set but novices often struggle with this tenacious Irish terrier's demands.
